neighbours.label: ' by' introducing a gerund that names the means of doing something (saved money by cooking), as opposed to agentive, locative or amount 'by'
fire: She paid off her loan early by working two jobs every summer.
You can lower your heating bill by sealing the gaps around windows.
He learned the language by watching films with subtitles.
The town cut traffic deaths by narrowing its busiest streets.
We kept the bread fresh by wrapping it in a damp cloth.
They raised the money by selling cakes at the market.
You can convert the fraction by dividing the top by the bottom.
The team won the game by scoring twice in the final minutes.

Your heating bill is sent by post at the end of each month.
He sat by the window watching the rain.

The bread was baked by her grandmother every Sunday.
The market is run by volunteers from the church.
The price of fuel went up by ten cents overnight.
The final was played in a stadium by the river.
